title: coldsplice-priming-flightlog-otis
content:
Coldsplice priming flightlog - quick brain dump (running experiments to understand transient latency/throughput when we rehydrate KV caches and re-warm tokenizers).

Context and motivation:
- Observed product A sees intermittent 200–800ms p99 spikes after long idle periods. Hypothesis: combination of cold KV cache + tokenizer lazy init + context prefill stalls. Need targeted microbench to reproduce and measure cost of various priming strategies.
- Goal: find cheap priming recipe that reduces p99 (tail) while keeping steady-state token cost low.

Testbed:
- Model: open-llama-7b-like (dense), served on rtx-a6000-equivalent.
- Runtime: local dev farm cluster node (prod-like build: runtime v1.18.3 feature-branch coldsplice).
- Input workload: 1) single-shot short prompts (avg 40 tokens), 2) chat-like conversational requests (avg 180 tokens).
- Arrival pattern: long-idle (30m idle), then burst ramp: 0 -> 150 QPS over 20s, hold 60s, ramp down. Repeated 12x.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server processing), QPS (successful), tokens/sec, GPU util, KV-cache hit-rate, number of tokenizer cold inits.

Commands used (local harness snippets):
- spawn load: ./bench/run_flow --profile coldsplice --qps 150 --ramp 20s --hold 60s --seed 42 
- capture traces: curl -sS http://localhost:8080/metrics > /tmp/metrics-coldsplice-prompts.txt
- restart runtime: ./devops/restart_node.sh --image runtime:feature/coldsplice

Experiment matrix (high level):
- baseline: no priming (fresh node after restart).
- prime-tokenizer-only: run 200 warmup requests that exercise tokenizer paths (many short inputs) before traffic begins.
- prime-kv-only: preload KV prefixes (run prefix cache filler that hits common prompt tokens).
- combined-prime: both tokenizer + kv prefill.
- selective-prime: prefill KV prefixes only for top-10 prefixes sampled from recent traffic.

Representative raw results (median of 6 runs each):
- baseline: p50=18ms, p95=210ms, p99=630ms, peak-qps-achieved=142, gpu-util=64%, kv-hit=12%
- prime-tokenizer-only: p50=20ms, p95=95ms, p99=180ms, peak-qps=148, gpu-util=66%, kv-hit=13%
- prime-kv-only: p50=19ms, p95=120ms, p99=260ms, peak-qps=146, gpu-util=65%, kv-hit=48%
- combined-prime: p50=21ms, p95=88ms, p99=140ms, peak-qps=150, gpu-util=69%, kv-hit=52%
- selective-prime: p50=20ms, p95=92ms, p99=155ms, peak-qps=149, gpu-util=68%, kv-hit=47%

Quick ASCII (p99 trend across phases)
- baseline:  [idle]---|spike:630|---steady 120s
- combined: [idle]---|spike:140|---steady 80s

Observations / interpretations:
1) Tokenizer init is surprisingly expensive for short prompts: prime-tokenizer-only reduced p99 by ~72% vs baseline. Likely lazy JIT / tokenizer memmap cost.
2) KV prefill improved throughput (higher peak-qps) and reduced some of the tail, but not as dramatic as tokenizer priming. KV hit-rate jump explains improved tokens/sec.
3) Combined priming yields the best tail behavior and highest peak QPS — additive effects.
4) Selective prefill (top-10 prefixes) gets ~90% of combined gains at ~20% of prefill cost (measured in extra tokens executed during priming). Good cost/benefit tradeoff.
5) p50 often slightly higher in primed runs — suggests priming introduces a constant baseline overhead (warm connection, GPU mem alloc), but reduces variance and big outliers. This is OK for our SLO if p99 reduces.

Cost accounting (very rough):
- Baseline extra cost (client-perceived) from p99 tail = user retries / timeouts; hard to monetize directly.
- Priming token budget: combined-prime used ~45k tokens per node per priming run. Selective-prime used ~9k tokens.
- Operational overhead: priming script time ~45s; small scheduling complexity.

Open questions / next steps:
- Where is tokenizer init happening? Need flame graphs (runtime + python c-ext). Add sampling profiler during warmup runs. Ticket: PLAT-3120.
- Are we over-priming memory objects that cause GC pauses? Monitor jemalloc stats and Python GC.
- Automate selective prefill list from rolling traffic window (last 6 hours). How often to refresh? Cost vs drift.
- Try priming at container-start vs pre-start sidecar (pre-warm outside main container) to avoid p50 increase.
- Explore micro-priming: do lightweight tokenizer touch (open mmap) without running tokens through full model. Might cut cost.

Immediate action items (for me):
- [ ] Add profiler capture to bench harness + paste flame graph link to PR. (target by 2024-12-08)
- [ ] Implement selective-preload pipeline: take top-k prefixes per region and feed to prefill agent. Draft proto in PR 482.
- [ ] Run cost-runbook comparison with finance (estimate tokens per month across fleet) and propose threshold for enabling selective priming.

Notes to self:
- Keep runs reproducible: always use seed + recorded traffic sample of 10k requests.
- Don't conflate client-side retry amplification with server-side processing — instrument client RTT separately.
- Check if tokenizer warmup triggers recompile of certain CPU kernels on host; ask infra about image build flags.

References / links:
- quick perf dashboard snapshot: grafana/dashboard/db/coldsplice-2024-11-17
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482 (draft: selective prefill agent)
- infra ticket: PLAT-3102 (node image warmup flags)

End of flightlog. Will iterate after profiling capture.

-- Otis
